title: A company anyone could own a piece of

probes.question: How could a VOC investor get their money back before the company ended?
options: Ask the company to repay it
Sell the share to someone else on the exchange

probes.question: True or false: shares in the VOC could be bought by any citizen of the Dutch Republic.

image.alt: A page from the Dutch East India Company records, a handwritten 1606 share receipt from the Enkhuizen chamber beside a page of dividend entries

body.question: The Dutch East India Company (VOC), founded in 1602, paid annual dividends for almost 200 years. About what share of its capital did they average each year?
body.reveal: About 18% of the capital a year. Any citizen of the Dutch Republic could buy shares, and shares could be bought and sold on secondary markets, one of which became the Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
